source.source: HYG v4.4 (Hipparcos-Yale-Gliese Database, D. Nash / astronexus)
source.epoch: ICRS/J2000 equinox; source astrometry primarily Hipparcos-2007 reduction, epoch J1991.25
source.sentinelDistDoc: dist == 100000.0 marks an unmeasurable/negative Hipparcos parallax; rows with it are dropped, not shipped.
source.hipSentinelDoc: hip == 0 means the row has no Hipparcos catalogue number.

galacticFrame.source: Hipparcos Catalogue vol. 1 §1.5.3 (ESA SP-1200, 1997); J2000 galactic frame constants shared by astropy and SOFA

panorama.title: The Milky Way panorama
panorama.longitudeConvention: l = 0 at the column centre, increasing leftward (sky seen from inside)
panorama.latitudeConvention: b = +90 at row 0, -90 at the last row

catalogRegistration.role: retained source record only; the photograph is registered astrometrically and owns visible stars

pointSourcePresentation.positionSource: licensed ESO photographic local maxima; no Google catalogue bytes
pointSourcePresentation.qualification: native fixed-size catalogue behavior collapsed into the prepared cubemap; point positions and colors remain ESO-derived

sky.qualification: source-photographed full sky sampled in ICRF through the J2000 galactic frame and the anchor-registered panorama; the scene registration carries the Moon pole and epoch; Solar System objects in the mosaic are capture artefacts; no Sun is baked into the cubemap
sky.sceneRegistrationChain: galactic -> ICRF (J2000 constants) -> body-fixed (IAU pole and prime meridian at the epoch) -> ecliptic presentation frame

analyticRadialFit.qualification: Least-squares fit to annular red-channel means from the bound native 128 by 128 Sun texture; fitted values only, no source pixels.

distanceScaling.qualification: The opaque photospheric core is projected from the IAU nominal solar radius and the object catalog's mean heliocentric distance. The retained glow profile remains a visual presentation; the distance is not epoch-specific.

provenance.source: VSOP87A heliocentric positions with IAU/WGCCRE rotation elements
provenance.qualification: Observed Moon Sun direction at 2026-09-03T00:00:00 TT, expressed in the ecliptic presentation frame (north up, Sun left at zero yaw) and in view space at the default camera pose.

controls.label: Visible color
controls.description: NASA CGI Moon Kit display map from LROC color imagery. Small gaps are inpainted; beyond 70° north/south, lower-resolution monochrome LOLA albedo replaces missing color. The app reduces saturation and adjusts tone for display.
controls.summary: Surface detail comes from LROC imagery. Small gaps are filled; monochrome replaces unavailable color near the poles.
controls.title: CGI Moon Kit surface mosaic

controls.label: Midnight temperature
controls.description: False-color bolometric temperature fitted to local midnight from Diviner observations in 2009–2022. Colors span 80–140 K, with endpoint colors beyond that range. Gray grid marks missing data and latitudes beyond ±70°. This combines many nights; it is not a current temperature map.
controls.summary: False-color temperature fitted to local midnight from 2009–2022 Diviner observations within ±70°. Gray grid marks unavailable data. This combines many nights, not current temperatures.
controls.title: LRO Diviner GHRM: midnight temperature

controls.label: Heat anomalies
controls.description: False-color difference between Diviner bolometric temperature at slope-adjusted midnight and a model of typical lunar soil. Blue is cooler and red warmer than the model; colors span −10 to +10 K. Observations cover 2009–2022 within ±70°; gray grid marks unavailable data. Residual terrain effects remain, and warm colors do not establish geothermal activity.
controls.summary: False-color difference from a typical-soil thermal model at slope-adjusted midnight, 2009–2022, within ±70°. Blue is cooler and red warmer; gray grid is unavailable. Residual terrain effects remain. Warm colors do not establish geothermal activity.
controls.title: LRO Diviner GHRM: heat anomalies

controls.label: Rock abundance
controls.description: Surface area covered by rocks, inferred with a rock-and-soil thermal model from Diviner observations in 2009–2022 at slope-adjusted midnight. Colors span 0–2%; larger fractions share the brightest color. Gray grid marks missing or physically invalid values and latitudes beyond ±70°. This estimates rock area, not individual boulder counts.
controls.summary: Modeled rock-area fraction from 2009–2022 Diviner observations at slope-adjusted midnight, within ±70°. Gray grid marks missing or physically invalid values. This estimates rock area, not individual boulder counts.
controls.title: LRO Diviner GHRM: rock abundance

controls.label: Elevation
controls.description: Numeric LOLA elevation above a 1,737.4 km reference sphere. Colors represent −12 to +12 km; this gridded laser-altimetry product includes interpolation and does not displace the globe or represent current illumination.
controls.summary: Colors show height above or below a 1,737.4 km sphere. Shading reveals slopes in the archived laser-altimeter measurements.
controls.title: LOLA LDEM16 elevation model

controls.label: Crust
controls.description: Crustal thickness inferred from GRAIL gravity and lunar topography under assumed crust and mantle densities. This is an interior model shown with shaded relief, not a direct observation of the crust.
controls.summary: Thickness is inferred from gravity and topography. The result depends on assumed rock densities, not direct underground imaging.
controls.title: Crustal-thickness model

controls.label: Silicate signature
controls.description: Diviner measures a thermal-infrared emissivity peak related to silicate composition. This 2021 map corrects viewing geometry and space weathering. Colors span 8.0–8.5 µm; values outside that range share endpoint colors. This is a composition proxy, not mineral abundance; residual topographic effects remain, especially above 50° latitude. Gray grid marks missing observations and latitudes beyond ±70°.
controls.title: Diviner Christiansen feature, 2009–2016

controls.label: Geology
controls.description: USGS interpreted geologic units from the 2020 unified map, version 2 (1:5,000,000). Colors distinguish mapped units and their relative ages; they are not photographed surface colors. Small units may be absent at this display scale.
